newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU officials meet over Albania.
newsitem.headline: EU officials meet over Albania.

text.p: Senior officials from the governments of the 15 European Union countries met on Thursday to try and hammer out a common stand to the growing crisis in the Balkans a day ahead of a visit by a high-level EU mission.

Diplomats said political directors from EU countries were examining reports from the head of the EU's mission in the Albanian capital Tirana and preparing the ground for a visit by Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo.

Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, whose country currently holds the EU's presidency, told reporters on Wednesday that Van Mierlo had been in contact with Albanian President Sali Berisha and would fly to Tirana on Friday to deliver a firm EU message.

With the Balkan country in turmoil, EU governments have so far failed to come up with a collective approach to the crisis, evoking uneasy memories of the inaction and failures which accompanied the run-up to the wars in former Yugoslavia.
The EU is expected to repeat calls to Berisha to open a political dialogue with the opposition, respect human and minority rights, and avoid bloodshed at all costs.
Albania's 11-party opposition Forum for Democracy has appealed to the United States and Europe to help the former Stalinist country find a political solution to avoid civil war.
"The state of public emergency must not be used to subvert these rights, freedom of expression must be maintained," said one EU diplomat shortly before the meeting started.
Between 1991-95 the EU pumped some $450 million dollars worth of economic assistance into the tiny country of some three million.
That made Albania the largest recipient of aid per head under the EU's PHARE programme for the development of former communist countries in central and eastern Europe.

Diplomats said some EU states wanted Berisha to be pressured into holding new elections under a new constitution and setting up a broad-based government, but it was not clear if these views would be formally presented.
At least 20 people have died in the unrest in Albania since the collapse of bogus investment funds.
